6. Draw-order check (brown #63, synthetic adjacent token)

Tests whether a station token near the badge can end up drawn on top of the enlarged badge under the CURRENT draw order (badge, then token pass), versus an alternate order (token, then badge).

Report

  1. Single-hit pop — exact scale/timing: 100% → 111% peak scale, attack 0–60ms (smoothstep) → settle to a 98.5% undershoot by 130ms → ease back to 100% (rest) by 260ms. No delay: the pop starts the instant the signal reaches the marker (same event that currently triggers the color flush).
  2. Coincidence (within 120ms window) — exact scale/timing: same curve shape, stronger peak: 100% → 117% by 60ms → 97.5% undershoot by 130ms → rest by 260ms. One pop, not two — driven by the existing selectBadgeHitReaction/mostRecentArrivalMs/BADGE_HIT_COINCIDENCE_WINDOW_MS (120ms) logic, unchanged, exactly as it already resolves the color-flush case today.
  3. Wobble: rotation, not translation. ±2° on solo (peak lean, then a −1° opposite correction before resting flat), ±3° / −1.5° on coincidence. No x/y translation was used — rotation around the badge's own computed center read as more "impact-like" and kept the badge from appearing to drift off its slot.
  4. Scale-only variant: yes, rendered (variant C in every keyframe/contact sheet above) — same 100%→111%→100% (solo) / 100%→117%→100% (coincidence) timing, with rotation zeroed out.
  5. Cramped-tile fixtures tested: Yellow #57 (compact single city), Green #14 (crowded 6-way hub), Brown #63 (fully-connected 6-edge hub), Gray #513 (fully-connected 6-edge hub), and the real #626 / canonical #8861 double-city fixture on its actual board hex, H18 (Philadelphia & Trenton OO). All five use real hexTileCatalog entries and real board coordinates from hexBoardData, not synthetic geometry.
  6. Collision/clipping issues found: no case where the enlarged badge's fill/border themselves clip against tile track, terrain text, or a city marker circle at either 111% or the 117% coincidence peak — margins are close on Brown #63 and Gray #513 (their 6-way hub track lines pass near the badge's slot) but never overlapping in these renders. The one clear collision found is a draw-order issue, not a geometry one — see #7.
  7. Was temporary draw-order elevation needed: yes, if a station token can ever sit adjacent to a badge's slot. The draw-order check (section 6) shows that under the CURRENT order — badge drawn during the tile pass, station tokens drawn afterward in a separate later pass (drawStationTokenPass(), confirmed called after all badge draws in HexGridRenderer.tsx) — a nearby token is painted on top of the popped badge and visibly covers part of its enlarged corner. The alternate order (token first, badge/pop last) keeps the popping badge fully visible. This is a real finding worth acting on if the mechanical pop is adopted, but per the brief nothing was changed in production to address it.
  8. Side-by-side references: section 1 (animated, real scale) and section 2 (5-frame keyframe contact sheets per fixture) above.
  9. Normal-scale animation-frame references: all of section 2 and the two GIFs in section 1 are rendered at the real DEFAULT_HEX_SIZE (42px) used in production — no magnification. Section 3's 3x crops are the separate "inspection" companion the brief allows, not a substitute for these.
  10. Near-concurrent-hit reference: sections 1 (animated) and 4 (keyframes + magnified peak crops).
  11. Visual assessment — no winner chosen:
    Color flush (current production): reads instantly as "this stop just paid" — the tint appears and fades smoothly, matches the traveling signal's own color language, and is essentially free of collision risk since it never changes the badge's footprint. At true gameplay scale the tint is present but subtle in a single still frame (visible clearly in the GIFs, less so in a paused frame).

    Mechanical pop (scale+wobble): reads more like a physical "hit," which matches the brief's intended framing ("the train hit this revenue stop"). The rotation wobble adds a touch of personality but is easy to miss at 42px in a still frame — it registers mainly in the animated version, and mainly on fixtures with less surrounding clutter (Yellow #57, the OO double-city) versus the busier 6-way hubs where the eye has more to scan. The coincidence-strength pop (117%) is more clearly distinguishable from the solo pop (111%) than the flush variant's tint-intensity difference is.

    Scale-only: cleaner and calmer than scale+wobble, and removes any residual concern about rotation reading as "jitter" on repeated hits to the same badge. It is also a bit less "eventful" than the full pop — whether that reads as more restrained (good) or less noticeable (less good) is exactly the kind of call this prototype was built to let you make directly rather than have decided for you.
  12. Production confirmation: no production file was modified. All rendering ran from a full verbatim copy of the relevant modules (hexCanvasPrimitives.ts, routeSignalGeometry.ts, routeLivery.ts, hexTileCatalog.ts, hexGeometry.ts, hexBoardData.ts) staged into an isolated scratch workspace outside the repository; the one code change (an optional pop transform parameter added to drawValueBadge) exists only in that scratch copy and was never written back to the repository.
  13. Test suite confirmation: the project's test suite was not run as part of this pass, per the brief — this was a visual-comparison-only prototype.

Exact constants used

Solo peak scale1.11 (111%)
Solo undershoot scale0.985 (98.5%)
Solo wobble+2° peak → −1° undershoot → 0° rest
Coincidence peak scale1.17 (117%)
Coincidence undershoot scale0.975 (97.5%)
Coincidence wobble+3° peak → −1.5° undershoot → 0° rest
Attack (rest → peak)0–60ms, smoothstep easing
Overshoot/correction (peak → undershoot)60–130ms, smoothstep easing
Settle (undershoot → rest)130–260ms, smoothstep easing
Total motion duration260ms (within the requested 220–300ms envelope)
Coincidence window (unchanged, reused)120ms (BADGE_HIT_COINCIDENCE_WINDOW_MS)
Badge fill/border/numberunchanged white/black/black at all times in the pop variant

This is a one-off comparison prototype, not a decision. Nothing in production — route-line colors, the traveling route signal, route geometry, signal speed, marker-based arrival timing, looping, revenue mapping, reduced-motion behavior, the color-flush code path, or the visual-flourish backlog — was changed. The scratch harness and its one code addition (a prototype-only pop parameter on drawValueBadge) live only in an isolated cloud workspace and were never staged back into the repository.
